dimensions.description: Source and target denote the same legally relevant object/work/event referent.
Source and target assert the same proposition, not merely adjacent metadata.
The subject/actor whose fact is asserted is preserved.
The fact is anchored to the same legally relevant use/acquisition/publication process or event.
Any legally relevant time meaning and trust level are preserved.
Legal qualifiers, scope, purpose, context, and conditions are preserved.
Value domains/cardinality can represent the IPEL proposition without coercive loss.
Descriptive evidence, permission/preference, trust, and legal/evaluative roles are not collapsed.
The IPEL proposition can be reconstructed without external inference or hidden state.
Equivalence does not depend on validation success, signer trust, rights preference, or legal inference.
The candidate semantic is defined in a current maintained normative specification, not only a custom/private extension.
